Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small dark spots appear on leaves and may develop into larger brown lesions. Fruits can also develop raised spots.
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.cause: Bacterial infection, commonly favored by warm and humid conditions.
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Remove badly infected leaves and fruits. Avoid working with plants when they are wet. Use appropriate bacterial disease management recommended for the crop.
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use healthy seeds, maintain good spacing, avoid overhead watering, and remove infected plant material.

Pepper__bell___healthy.symptoms: No major visible symptoms of disease detected.
Pepper__bell___healthy.prevention: Continue proper watering, sunlight, nutrition, and regular monitoring.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings appear on older leaves, often surrounded by yellowing.
Potato___Early_blight.cause: Fungal infection caused by Alternaria species.
Potato___Early_blight.treatment: Remove infected plant material and use suitable fungicide management when necessary.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Practice crop rotation, avoid prolonged leaf wetness, provide good spacing, and remove infected debris.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: No major visible symptoms of disease detected.
Potato___healthy.prevention: Maintain proper irrigation, nutrition, sunlight, and regular crop inspection.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Dark water-soaked lesions can appear on leaves and may rapidly expand under cool and wet conditions.
Potato___Late_blight.cause: Disease caused by the oomycete Phytophthora infestans.
Potato___Late_blight.treatment: Remove severely infected material and use appropriate late-blight management products when required.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Use healthy planting material, improve air circulation, avoid prolonged leaf wetness, and monitor crops regularly.

Tomato_Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small dark lesions appear on leaves, stems, and sometimes fruits.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.cause: Bacterial infection favored by warm and wet conditions.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.treatment: Remove infected plant material and follow appropriate bacterial disease management practices.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use disease-free seeds, avoid overhead irrigation, maintain spacing, and remove infected debris.

Tomato_Early_blight.symptoms: Brown circular lesions with concentric rings develop on older leaves and may cause leaf yellowing.
Tomato_Early_blight.cause: Fungal infection caused by Alternaria species.
Tomato_Early_blight.treatment: Remove infected leaves and use appropriate fungicide management when necessary.
Tomato_Early_blight.prevention: Use crop rotation, good plant spacing, proper watering, and remove infected plant debris.

Tomato_healthy.symptoms: No major visible symptoms of disease detected.
Tomato_healthy.prevention: Maintain proper watering, sunlight, nutrition, and regular monitoring.

Tomato_Late_blight.symptoms: Dark water-soaked lesions can develop rapidly on leaves and stems, especially during cool and wet conditions.
Tomato_Late_blight.treatment: Remove severely infected material and use appropriate late-blight management when required.
Tomato_Late_blight.prevention: Improve air circulation, avoid prolonged leaf wetness, use healthy planting material, and monitor crops regularly.

Tomato_Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Yellow patches may appear on the upper leaf surface with olive or grayish fungal growth underneath.
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.cause: Fungal infection favored by high humidity.
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.treatment: Remove affected leaves and improve ventilation. Use appropriate fungicide management when necessary.
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.prevention: Reduce humidity, improve air circulation, avoid wetting leaves, and provide adequate plant spacing.

Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Small circular spots with dark borders and pale centers appear mainly on older leaves.
Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.cause: Fungal infection caused by Septoria species.
Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.treatment: Remove infected leaves and use suitable fungicide management when necessary.
Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Avoid overhead watering, improve air circulation, rotate crops, and remove infected plant debris.

Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.symptoms: Leaves may develop yellow speckling, bronzing, and fine webbing when infestations become severe.
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.cause: Feeding damage caused by two-spotted spider mites.
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.treatment: Remove heavily infested leaves and use appropriate mite-management methods.
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.prevention: Monitor plants regularly, control weeds, maintain plant health, and encourage beneficial insects where appropriate.

Tomato__Target_Spot.symptoms: Brown circular lesions with concentric rings can develop on leaves and fruits.
Tomato__Target_Spot.cause: Fungal infection caused by Corynespora cassiicola.
Tomato__Target_Spot.treatment: Remove infected material and use suitable fungicide management when necessary.
Tomato__Target_Spot.prevention: Improve air circulation, avoid prolonged leaf wetness, maintain spacing, and remove infected debris.

Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Leaves may show mottled light and dark green patterns, distortion, and reduced plant growth.
Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.cause: Viral infection caused by Tomato mosaic virus.
Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.treatment: There is no direct cure for viral infection. Remove infected plants and control sources of spread.
Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Use clean tools and healthy planting material, wash hands before handling plants, and remove infected plants.

Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.symptoms: Leaves may curl upward, become yellow, and plants may show stunted growth.
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.cause: Viral disease commonly transmitted by whiteflies.
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.treatment: There is no direct cure for infected plants. Remove severely infected plants and manage the insect vector.
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.prevention: Monitor and manage whiteflies, use healthy seedlings, remove infected plants, and control weeds around the crop.
